items.text: Abelian varieties over $\mathbb C$: complex compact tori $\mathbb C^n/\Lambda$, $\Lambda$ of rank $2n$ (rigidity).
Smooth connected affine group = extension of a semisimple group by its solvable radical.

Semisimple groups: up to isogeny (division by a finite central subgroup) a finite product of simple groups; classified by root systems, independently of the characteristic over an algebraically closed field (Borel's notes, Chevalley's seminar).
Radical = extension of a torus by a unipotent group.
\text{torus}\ \mathbb G_m^{\,r}\ (\text{twisted over a non-closed field by the Galois action on the dual lattice});\qquad \text{unipotent}=\text{successive extensions of }\mathbb G_a^{\,r}
How the additive groups fit together in unipotent groups is not well understood.
Simple pieces of commutative groups: $\mathbb G_m$, $\mathbb G_a$, abelian varieties, $\mathbb Z/p$ (constant or twisted finite groups), $\mu_p$, $\alpha_p$.
